request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Ledgerpoint
- Target role: Backend Engineer, Payments
- Seniority: mid
- Key skills to assess: Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, event-driven architecture, idempotency, exactly-once processing, observability, strangler-fig migrations, property-based testing
- Focus areas: payment systems, concurrency and correctness, invoicing and reconciliation, webhook handling, distributed systems reliability

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.skill: Idempotency and exactly-once processing in payment systems
slots.intent: Assess ability to design and reason about idempotent payment operations, understand the guarantees offered by different architectures, and handle duplicate requests safely.
key_points: Idempotency key generation, storage, and retrieval strategy
Exactly-once semantics vs. at-least-once delivery and compensating transactions
Race conditions between checking and writing (check-then-act antipattern)
Handling retries without side effects (e.g., charging twice)
State machine design for payment lifecycle to prevent invalid transitions

slots.skill: Event-driven architecture with Kafka and webhook reliability
slots.intent: Evaluate ability to build resilient event-driven systems, manage message ordering and replayability, and handle webhook delivery failures and out-of-order events.
key_points: Partition key selection for ordering guarantees and consumer group semantics
Dead-letter queues and retry strategies for webhook delivery
Webhook signature verification, timeout handling, and exponential backoff
Event schema versioning and backwards compatibility
Ordering guarantees vs. scalability tradeoffs (single partition vs. partitioned topics)

slots.skill: Observability and debugging in distributed payment flows
slots.intent: Determine how the candidate approaches monitoring, tracing, and troubleshooting complex payment reconciliation and invoicing workflows across multiple services.
key_points: Distributed tracing (correlation IDs, span hierarchy) to track payment lifecycle
Logging strategy for compliance and auditing (what to log, PII masking)
Metrics selection for payment success rate, latency, and failure modes
Diagnosing eventual consistency issues and reconciliation gaps
Alerting thresholds and on-call runbooks for common payment failures
